question: What is the unit of measurement used for measuring the energy requirement of the human body?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Calories**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Calories** are the unit of measurement used to quantify the amount of energy the human body requires and expends.
 
• It represents the amount of energy obtained from food and beverages and the energy consumed by the body for various physical activities and metabolic processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Erg**:

 
 
• A unit of energy in the centimetre-gram-second (CGS) system, but it is very small and not commonly used for measuring energy in biological systems.
 
 
 
• **Ohm**:
 
 
• A unit of electrical resistance, not related to energy or the human body's energy needs.
 
 
 
• **Joule**:
 
 
• The SI unit of energy. While joules can measure energy, **calories** are more commonly used to express the energy content of food and the energy requirement of the human body. (1 calorie = 4.184 joules).
